Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

space noun

room; an empty area

also room, make room, gap, empty space

classical

Caes. BC 3.92.1: tantum erat relictum spatiī
Lucr. 1.426: locus ac spatium, quod ināne vocāmus

spatium, spatiī n.

noun, second declension

space, room; the distance between

The room or extent a thing has, or the distance between things; also a space of time (see period).

Other words

  • locus, locī m. — room, a place for someone or something

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Poen. 23: līberīs ut sit locus

    Room for someone: est locus, there is room; locum ad spectandum dare, to give someone a place to watch from (Cic. Mur. 73, Lewis & Short).

  • intervallum, intervallī n. — a gap, the space between two things

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 7.23.1: paribus intervallīs (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Inter duās aciēs tantum erat relictum spatiī, ut satis esset ad concursum utriusque exercitūs.

    Between the two lines enough space had been left for each army to charge.Caes. BC 3.92.1

  • servī nē obsideant, līberīs ut sit locus

    slaves must not take up the seats, so that there is room for free menPlaut. Poen. 23

See also space, position, room, period.
